    Parse one or several references in APA 7 format

    parse_apa_text.Rd

    Extracts metadata (authors, year, title, DOI) from one or several bibliographic references in APA 7 format, from free text.

    Usage

    parse_apa_text(input, as_ref_df = FALSE, source_file_label = "APA_Input")

    Arguments

    input

    One of the following formats:

    • a path to a text file (character(1) ending with ".txt"), one reference per line ;

    • a character vector, one reference per element ;

    • a single-column data.frame or tibble, one reference per line.

    as_ref_df

    Logical. If TRUE, returns a data frame formatted specifically for use with validate_references(). This adds columns ref_n, source_file, and converts authorships into a list column authors_list compatible with the validation pipeline. Defaults to FALSE.

    source_file_label

    Character string. Used only if as_ref_df = TRUE. Sets the value for the source_file column in the output. Defaults to "APA_Input".

    Value

    Depending on as_ref_df:

    If FALSE (default)

    A data.frame with one row per reference and the columns:

    title

    character. Title extracted from the reference, or NA if the splitting pattern could not be identified.

    doi

    character. Normalized DOI (lowercase, without URL prefix), extracted only if it appears as a https://doi.org/... URL at the very end of the reference ; NA otherwise.

    publication_year

    numeric. Publication year extracted from the (YYYY) pattern ; NA if absent or malformed.

    authorships

    character. Concatenated string of authors in the format "Last name, First name; Last name, First name; ...", or NA if no author could be identified before the year.

    authorships_list

    list of data.frame. For each reference, a two-column data.frame (first_name, last_name), one row per detected author (empty data.frame with 0 rows if no author could be extracted).

    If TRUE

    A tibble compatible with validate_references(), containing:

    source_file

    character. The label provided via source_file_label.

    ref_n

    integer. Sequential reference number.

    title

    character. Extracted title.

    doi

    character. Extracted DOI.

    year

    numeric. Extracted publication year.

    authors

    character. String of authors (same as authorships above).

    authors_list

    list. List of data.frames with first_name and last_name columns.

    Limitations of the approach

    This function relies on an extraction by regular expressions based on the expected structure of an APA 7 reference (Authors (Year). Title. Journal, ...). It does not rely on any robust grammatical parser and assumes that references are correctly and strictly formatted:

    • non-standard punctuation (missing or misplaced comma or period, extra space) may prevent the correct extraction of a field (authors, title, year) ;

    • the year must appear explicitly in the form (YYYY) or (YYYYa) ; any other form (e.g. "n.d.", "in press", year range) will not be recognized and will return NA ;

    • the title is split at the first period following the year: a title containing an abbreviation, an internal period, or preceded by an atypical author structure may be truncated or incorrectly extracted ;

    • the DOI is only recognized as a doi.org URL placed at the very end of the string ; a DOI mentioned in another form (e.g. "DOI: 10.xxxx/...", DOI in the middle of the text) will not be detected ;

    • authors are extracted via a Last name, Initials pattern ; non-standard formats (ambiguous compound names, initials without a period, first name-last name order) may produce incomplete or erroneous results.

    In case of non-compliance with the expected format, the function generally does not generate an explicit error: the affected fields are silently set to NA or partially extracted. It is therefore recommended to visually check the results rather than assuming 100% reliable extraction, especially on heterogeneous or variable-quality corpora of references.

    See also

    check_doi_exists() to validate the existence of an extracted DOI, validate_references() for the full reference validation pipeline via OpenAlex/DOI, format_apa_for_validation() to convert existing results.

    Examples

    # Nominal case: well-formatted reference
parse_apa_text("Smith, J. (2020). Title of paper. Journal, 12(3), 45-67.
https://doi.org/10.1234/xyz")
#>                                                                           raw_reference
#> 1 Smith, J. (2020). Title of paper. Journal, 12(3), 45-67.\nhttps://doi.org/10.1234/xyz
#>            title         doi publication_year authorships authorships_list
#> 1 Title of paper 10.1234/xyz             2020    Smith, J         J, Smith

refs <- c(
  "Smith, J. (2020). Title one. Journal, 12(3), 45-67.",
  "Doe, J., & Roe, R. (2019). Title two. Journal, 5(1), 1-10."
)
parse_apa_text(refs)
#>                                                raw_reference     title  doi
#> 1        Smith, J. (2020). Title one. Journal, 12(3), 45-67. Title one <NA>
#> 2 Doe, J., & Roe, R. (2019). Title two. Journal, 5(1), 1-10. Title two <NA>
#>   publication_year    authorships authorships_list
#> 1             2020       Smith, J         J, Smith
#> 2             2019 Doe, J; Roe, R   J, R, Doe, Roe

# Directly format for validation pipeline
parse_apa_text(refs, as_ref_df = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   raw_reference         source_file ref_n title doi    year authors authors_list
#>   <chr>                 <chr>       <int> <chr> <chr> <dbl> <chr>   <list>      
#> 1 Smith, J. (2020). Ti… APA_Input       1 Titl… NA     2020 Smith,… <df [1 × 2]>
#> 2 Doe, J., & Roe, R. (… APA_Input       2 Titl… NA     2019 Doe, J… <df [2 × 2]>

# Edge case: non-compliant format (missing year) -> partial extraction
parse_apa_text("Smith J Title of paper without proper APA formatting")
#>                                          raw_reference title  doi
#> 1 Smith J Title of paper without proper APA formatting  <NA> <NA>
#>   publication_year authorships authorships_list
#> 1               NA        <NA>
